overview: This Senate resolution supports naming September 11 through 17, 2025, as "Patriot Week." The week runs from the anniversary of the September 11, 2001, attacks to Constitution Day on September 17, the date the Constitution was signed in 1787. The resolution lists founding documents, historic speeches, flags and figures from American history, from the Founders to Harriet Tubman and Martin Luther King Jr. It encourages citizens, schools and all levels of government to honor and study U.S. history and founding principles during the week. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 15, 2025.
for: Supporters say setting aside a week to study the nation's founding documents and history helps citizens understand shared values and honors the victims of the September 11 attacks.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it doesn't change any law, fund civics education, or require any school to take part.
